tested.title: Race the receiver-lock branch
tested.question: Do the lock split and the parallel final pass make small fresh copies faster, and do extra receiving workers now help?
tested.measure: LK1 on the Mac-mars link: parent 21ae6844 against 4c5c425c (engine/receiver-locks), default, --no-atomic and -j8; small-flat, small-deep, real-congress; fresh and no-op; time to durable, 8 blocks.

buildable.title: Re-measure no-op syncs
buildable.question: Where does a no-op re-sync spend its time once the receiver fixes land?
buildable.measure: real-congress and real-psample no-op, push and pull, against rsync; user and kernel time on each end.
buildable.evidence: H21: congress no-op push ran at 0.74x rsync's speed, with 408.8 s of CPU against 18.8 s. MA7's pull deficit came from destination path walks.

trees.question: What limits xs's small-file fresh copies once the receiver's global lock and serial final pass are gone, and what removes the next limit?
Where does a re-sync that changes nothing spend its time, and can it skip unchanged subtrees?

history.text: $0.08: No race finished this slot. The lab races still show xs-cpp well behind xs-rs on small-file fresh copies, for example small-deep fresh push at 24.037 s against 9.84 s (ratio 0.409). Next we race the receiver-lock branch (4c5c425c against 21ae6844) on small-flat, small-deep and real-congress, then re-profile no-op re-syncs on the result; negative zstd levels are a low-priority side change.

started: Small-file fresh copies are where xs-cpp trails most. Lab races: small-deep.fresh.mac-mars.sender at 24.037 s against xs-rs 9.84 s (rs_vs_cpp 0.409); small-flat.fresh.mac-mars.sender at 13.302 s against 6.528 s (0.491); real-congress.fresh.mac-mars.sender at 32.594 s against 14.723 s (0.452). The branch is already built, so the cost is only race time. Its result also gates A2-A7 and the start point for B1.

$0.07: No race finished this slot; the lab races still show xs-cpp well behind xs-rs on small-file fresh copies (small-deep push 24.037 s vs 9.84 s, ratio 0.409). Next we race A1 (receiver-lock branch c5b765eb54fc), then re-profile no-op re-syncs (B1) on the result. Negative zstd levels (C5) are a low-priority side change.

started: This is lower expected gain on the lab's current workloads. The races are fresh copies on a 10G link where xs-cpp is CPU-bound and trails xs-rs (e.g. small-deep push 24.037 s vs 9.84 s), and Z1 showed level 3 slowing the 10 GbE copy below no compression. Still, it is small, self-contained, and the only buildable change.
